confidenceNote: This is characterisation, not measurement, and it is written to be recognised rather than to be true. It reads like an Enneagram or a star sign on purpose: entertaining, occasionally sharp, and no more evidence-based than either. The relationship lines are about levers and how they rub against each other, not about people. Nothing here is advice and nothing here diagnoses anybody.
note: Keyed by class id. `origins` are OFFERED, never asserted — see the warning below, which the page is required to print alongside them.
originsWarning: Nothing here knows anything about your childhood. Five questions about money cannot see it, and a tool that told you what your parents were like would be making it up. These are the stories people who build this way most often say they recognise. Pick the one that lands, pick none, and know that recognising one says something about you and nothing about whether it happened.

earner.headline: You go at the number directly.
earner.coreDesire: To be worth more this year than last, and to have it acknowledged in writing.
earner.coreFear: Being quietly underpaid for years by people who like you very much.
earner.lie: If I do outstanding work, somebody will notice and fix my salary.
earner.truth: They will notice. They will not fix it. It gets fixed when you ask, and almost never otherwise.
earner.atBest: You turn capability into leverage without apology, and you make asking normal for everyone around you. You have raised other people's pay just by saying your own number out loud in front of them.
earner.atWorst: Your self-worth and your salary become the same number, so a bad review is an identity crisis. You work through every warning sign because stopping feels like losing ground.
earner.blindSpot: Earning more and spending more is standing still at speed. You can out-earn almost anything except your own lifestyle.

growth.why: A pound kept is worth more than a pound earned, because nobody taxes it twice. Learning that one thing turns a good earner into a wealthy one.

stress.why: When the raise does not come, patience curdles into shortcuts, and the shortcut is always a bet you have not sized.

partner.why: You make it, they keep it, and neither of you can do the other's half. This is the least glamorous and most effective pairing on the list.

friend.why: Same restlessness, different lever. They will talk you into asking for more and you will talk them into finishing something.

annoying.why: Their caution reads to you as timidity. It is not — it is the floor that would let you take a real swing — but it will still make your teeth itch.

wary.why: They are doing nothing, slowly, and getting richer than you. Nothing exposes a hustler like somebody winning by waiting.

triggeredBy.why: They talk about assets in a tone that suggests you should already own some. You will feel behind, and behind makes you buy things.

weakTo.why: It does not attack your income — it grows to match it. Every raise feeds it, and you never notice because nothing ever gets worse.

people.who: The manager who says “we’ll revisit it” and genuinely means to
people.why: Unkindness you could fight. Warmth makes you wait, and waiting is the whole cost.

people.who: Somebody your age who is visibly further ahead
people.why: You do not get faster. You get less careful, and you buy something to feel level.

people.who: A recruiter who calls in a bad week
people.why: You will take the call in the mood rather than in the plan, and the mood is always cheaper than you are.

circumstances.when: The month a raise actually lands
circumstances.why: It is committed before it clears. You have had four raises and the same amount of money.

circumstances.when: A new title with no number attached to it
circumstances.why: It feels like the win and it postpones the win, and you will not notice for eighteen months.

circumstances.when: Being the best-paid person in a small room
circumstances.why: You stop asking, because you have won a league you did not mean to enter.

origins.house: The house where somebody worked constantly and it was still tight
origins.detail: You learned that effort is the lever, because you watched it be the only one available.

origins.house: The house where being good was how you earned your place
origins.detail: Achievement and safety got wired together early. Salary is just the adult version of the report card.

origins.house: The house where somebody was passed over and never got over it
origins.detail: You are determined not to be the person who was loyal and quietly left behind.

earner.needsToHear: You are allowed to stop climbing for a year and keep what you have already got. That is not laziness — it is the only way any of this becomes money rather than income.

sign.name: The Forge
sign.ruledBy: Mars, who has never once waited

patron.name: The Ledger That Reads Back
patron.pact: It shows you what everyone else is paid. It will not tell you whether you are happy, and it has never been asked.

earner.curse: You will always know, to the pound, what you are worth — and never once feel it.
vulnerabilities: Praise offered instead of a number
Any raise, in the month it lands

good: You said a number out loud and did not immediately apologise for it
Somebody else asked for more because they watched you do it
A month where your income rose and your spending did not
ill: Three years of the same job title
A raise you have already spent
Being the best-paid person in a very small room

earner.reading: Mars is loud in your chart and has been for years, which is why you keep moving and why you are tired. This is a season for consolidation rather than conquest: the thing you are chasing has already been caught twice and set down again without being noticed. Somebody will offer you recognition in place of money. Recognise it, thank them, and ask again anyway.

roles.first: Effort is your main instrument. More money arriving is your answer to almost every question, and it is a genuinely good answer — it is simply the one you reach for before you have checked whether the question was about arriving or about leaving.
roles.second: Underneath whatever you present as, you privately believe you could out-earn the problem. It is what you reach for at two in the morning, and it is why you find being stuck unbearable rather than merely annoying.
roles.third: It is what people meet first — the drive, the plans, the sense that you are going somewhere. Some of it is real and some of it is a coat you put on in rooms, and you cannot always tell which.
roles.shadow: You almost never pull this lever. Everything gets solved by cutting or by investing, and the largest number on your page has sat unnegotiated for years. Watch for: a decade of quiet excellence, a salary that moved with inflation and not a step further, and the sense that you did everything right.

keeper.headline: You find money by removing things.
keeper.coreDesire: To never be the mug. To never look back and find you were quietly paying for something you did not use.
keeper.coreFear: Waste. Being taken advantage of by somebody who counted on you not checking.
keeper.lie: I can cut my way to being comfortable.
keeper.truth: There is a floor to cutting and no ceiling to earning. You will hit yours and then keep sanding, because sanding feels like progress.
keeper.atBest: Every pound in your life is doing a job you chose for it. You are the person a recession barely touches, and you are unbothered by things other people find frightening.
keeper.atWorst: You spend forty minutes saving four pounds and never once ask for a raise. Frugality becomes a personality, and everyone around you has to live inside it.
keeper.blindSpot: The biggest number on your page is your income, and you have never once negotiated it. You are optimising the small column.

growth.why: One uncomfortable conversation is worth more than a decade of cancelled subscriptions, and you already have the discipline to keep what it brings.

stress.why: Cutting stops being strategy and becomes flinching. You hoard, you deploy nothing, and you call the fear prudence.

partner.why: They raise the ceiling, you defend the floor. Left alone they inflate and you stagnate; together neither happens.

friend.why: You are the only two who find a spreadsheet soothing. They will never make you justify not spending money.

annoying.why: They lose in an evening what you saved over a year, and then tell a very good story about it.

wary.why: They commit to enormous irreversible things with a calm that alarms you. You cannot un-buy a house.

triggeredBy.why: It is not the risk. It is the swagger about the risk, from somebody who has never read a terms page.

weakTo.why: It cannot touch anyone who asks. You do not ask, so it feeds for years while you are busy being excellent at not spending.

people.who: Anyone who calls you tight, lightly, in front of others
people.why: It lands far harder than they will ever know, and you will overspend within the fortnight to prove something to nobody.

people.who: A salesperson offering a discount you did not ask for
people.why: The saving is real, which is exactly the problem. You will buy a thing you did not want at a price you cannot fault.

people.who: The friend who never checks a price and seems fine
people.why: You will conclude the checking was the mistake rather than that they earn more.

circumstances.when: A sale with a deadline on it
circumstances.why: Your whole defence is deliberation and the deadline is designed to remove it.

circumstances.when: A pay review you do not prepare for
circumstances.why: You will accept the first number, having spent the year saving a fraction of what you just left behind.

circumstances.when: Any decision where the cheapest option is genuinely worse
circumstances.why: You are excellent at price and untrained at cost, and here they point in opposite directions.

origins.house: The house where the bills were opened at the table
origins.detail: You knew the state of things before you could read them, and you have been counting ever since.

origins.house: The house where somebody spent it and somebody else went without
origins.detail: You learned that waste is not neutral. Somebody always pays for it, and it was not the person spending.

origins.house: The house where being careful was the highest compliment available
origins.detail: Thrift was not a strategy there, it was a virtue — and virtues are much harder to put down when they stop working.

keeper.needsToHear: You have already won the hard half. The half you are avoiding is one conversation long, and you are the person best equipped to keep what it produces.

sign.name: The Sieve
sign.season: The last three days of the month

patron.name: The Unopened Envelope
patron.pact: Nothing gets past you. In exchange, you will never be able to leave a bill unread, including on holiday.

keeper.curse: You will find the leak every time and never once look at the size of the tap.
resistances: Being sold to by anyone at all
vulnerabilities: Any saving that costs an hour to make

good: You cancelled something and did not miss it once
A month where the fixed costs went down and the life did not
You negotiated something without rehearsing it first
ill: Forty minutes spent saving four pounds
A pay review you did not attend
Somebody else in the house hiding a purchase from you

keeper.reading: Mercury governs you and Mercury is interested in detail rather than scale, which is both your gift and the whole problem. You have swept every corner of a room you did not choose the size of. There is a conversation available to you this season that is worth more than a decade of the work you are currently doing, and you will find nine reasons to have it later.

roles.first: You run your life on what leaves rather than what arrives, and it works — you keep more of every pound than almost anyone. The cost is that you can spend a year sanding a floor and never once look at the ceiling.
roles.second: It is your fallback when things tighten. The first instinct in a bad month is to cut, and you are good at it, which is exactly why you sometimes cut when you should have asked.
roles.third: People read you as careful, and mostly mean it as a compliment. It is also why nobody tells you about anything expensive until it is decided.
roles.shadow: Almost nothing leaves your attention. Money arrives, money goes, and the gap is a feeling rather than a figure. Watch for: an income that has doubled, a life that feels the same, and no honest answer to where the difference went.

builder.headline: You see a business where other people see an offer.
builder.coreDesire: To owe nobody anything, and to have income that does not depend on one person liking you.
builder.coreFear: A single point of failure. One employer, one client, one decision-maker who could end it on a Tuesday.
builder.lie: Once this thing is mine, I will finally be safe.
builder.truth: You can build yourself a job with a worse boss and no sick pay. Ownership is not the same as security, and sometimes it is the opposite.
builder.atBest: You make options out of nothing. When something collapses you are the one person in the room who already has three other things running.
builder.atWorst: Six half-built projects, none finished, all of them described as optionality. You are avoiding the boring part and calling it strategy.
builder.blindSpot: You start things to feel free and end up with more masters than you had before. Every unfinished project is a small debt of attention.

growth.why: Finishing one thing and letting it run beats starting a fourth. The patience you find dull is the exact skill that would make any of this compound.

stress.why: Money gets tight and you go back for a salary — which is fine — but you do it resentfully, which makes you bad at both.

partner.why: They are the reason you can afford to be wrong. Every good risk-taker has somebody boring holding the floor, and it is not a coincidence.

friend.why: They believe you before you have proved anything, which is worth more in the first year than any advice.

annoying.why: You are trying to build something and they want to talk about your broadband bill.

wary.why: Their patience makes your energy look like flailing, and privately you suspect they might be right.

triggeredBy.why: Asking what happens if it fails is a reasonable question that will make you defensive every single time.

weakTo.why: It is built for you specifically. Be your own boss, own your time, unlimited ceiling — every word of the pitch is aimed at the thing you already want.

people.who: Anyone who says “you should sell that”
people.why: You will start a fourth thing that evening. It is the nicest sentence in the world and it costs you a year.

people.who: A first customer who wants it slightly different
people.why: You will rebuild it for them, for free, and call it product-market fit.

people.who: Somebody successful who says your idea is nearly right
people.why: Nearly is the hook. You will spend six months chasing their version of it rather than shipping yours.

circumstances.when: The week something almost works
circumstances.why: Almost is more addictive than working. Working is quiet; almost is electric and it never ends.

circumstances.when: A quiet month at the day job
circumstances.why: The energy has to go somewhere and it will go into starting rather than finishing.

circumstances.when: Being asked what you do, at a party
circumstances.why: You will describe the newest thing, out loud, and having described it you will owe it your next three months.

origins.house: The house where somebody loyal got let go anyway
origins.detail: You concluded early that safety through employment is a story, and you have been building an exit ever since.

origins.house: The house where you made your own fun and your own money
origins.detail: Nobody was going to hand you anything, so you got very good at making things out of not much.

origins.house: The house where someone else's decisions ran everything
origins.detail: You learned what it feels like when your life turns on somebody else's mood. You have been building away from that ever since.

builder.needsToHear: Finish one. Not the best one — any one. A finished small thing teaches you more than four brilliant unfinished ones, and it is the only thing that ever compounds.

sign.name: The Workshop
sign.ruledBy: An unnamed star, catalogued twice and lost both times
sign.card: The Magician, tools laid out, none picked up

patron.name: The Door You Built Yourself
patron.pact: It opens onto anywhere. It does not lock, it has no walls attached, and you must keep building it forever or it is simply a door in a field.

builder.curse: Everything you start is yours. So is everything you do not finish.
vulnerabilities: Being asked what you do at a party

good: Somebody paid you, once, for anything
A thing you built ran for a week without you touching it
You said no to a good idea because you were finishing a better one
ill: Four projects, all at seventy per cent
A domain name bought at midnight
Explaining optionality to somebody who did not ask

builder.reading: Your ruling star is uncatalogued, which suits you and explains the difficulty. Fire in mutable season means enormous ignition and very little containment. The work this month is not a new fire — it is a lid. Somebody will show you an opportunity that is genuinely good and it is still, this season, a trap, because it is the fourth one.

roles.first: You make money by making things. It is the lever with no ceiling and the worst hourly rate for the first two years, and you are constitutionally unable to stop reaching for it.
roles.second: It runs underneath the day job as a permanent private plan. Half your good ideas arrive while you are being paid to think about something else.
roles.third: People assume you have something on the side, and they are usually right. It makes you interesting at parties and slightly unreliable on a Wednesday.
roles.shadow: Every pound you receive comes from exactly one place, and one person's decision could end it. Watch for: a job you would not choose being the only thing you have, and no answer at all to the question of what you would do on Monday.

compounder.headline: You would rather your money did the work.
compounder.coreDesire: To be right slowly, and to have the arithmetic prove it eventually.
compounder.coreFear: Being old and poor because you did the sensible thing too late.
compounder.lie: If I get the allocation right, everything else takes care of itself.
compounder.truth: For the first decade your savings rate matters far more than your fund choice. You are polishing the small lever with great precision.
compounder.atBest: You are the calmest person in a crash. Everyone else is selling and you are doing nothing, on purpose, and it is the single most valuable thing anyone does with money.
compounder.atWorst: You optimise instead of living. The spreadsheet becomes the point, and you are quietly insufferable about other people's decisions.
compounder.blindSpot: You have modelled thirty years and not asked for a raise in four. The input is bigger than the return, early on, and you find the input boring.

growth.why: Nothing you do to the portfolio in year one matters as much as what you put into it. Raising the input is the highest-return move you have available and you have never tried it.

stress.why: Patience gets boring, boredom becomes tinkering, and tinkering wearing a spreadsheet is still gambling.

partner.why: They produce the input, you handle the machine. Neither of you finds the other's half interesting, which is exactly why it works.

friend.why: You are the only two who measure in decades. You will disagree permanently about bricks versus screens and neither of you will ever be in a hurry about it.

annoying.why: They get in three years late, do everything wrong, and occasionally win — and they will tell you about it.

wary.why: You cannot model them. Their returns come from something you have no spreadsheet for, and that is genuinely unsettling.

triggeredBy.why: Being told that bricks are real and your holdings are just numbers on a screen. You will argue. You will not enjoy it.

weakTo.why: It does not need you to be reckless. It only needs you to be bored, competent, and convinced you could do slightly better than the index.

people.who: The friend up three hundred per cent who mentions it lightly
people.why: Lightly is the load-bearing word. You will not copy them; you will just start looking, which is the same thing eleven months later.

people.who: Anyone with a slightly better spreadsheet
people.why: You will rebuild yours instead of raising the amount going into it.

people.who: Somebody who retired early and will not say quite how
people.why: The gap in the story is where you put your own worst guess.

circumstances.when: A flat year
circumstances.why: Nothing has gone wrong, which your temperament reads as nothing working, and you will fix a machine that is not broken.

circumstances.when: An afternoon with the fund documents and no plans
circumstances.why: You will find a nine-basis-point improvement and spend a weekend on it while your salary sits unnegotiated for a fourth year.

circumstances.when: A fall that lasts longer than four months
circumstances.why: You are built for the crash and not for the grind. It is month seven, not week one, that gets people like you.

origins.house: The house where somebody explained interest to you and it stuck
origins.detail: You met the idea early that time does the heavy lifting, and it reorganised how you see almost everything.

origins.house: The house where somebody sold at the bottom
origins.detail: You saw fear cost real money once, and you decided very young that you would be the one who did not flinch.

origins.house: The house where waiting was rewarded
origins.detail: Patience actually paid off for you as a child, which is rarer than it sounds and is most of why you can do this at all.

compounder.needsToHear: The spreadsheet is finished. It has been finished for a while. The thing you are avoiding is the conversation about your salary, and it is worth more than every optimisation in it.

sign.name: The Long Orbit
sign.ruledBy: Jupiter, who is in no hurry and never has been
sign.hour: Any Tuesday; they are all the same Tuesday
sign.card: The Wheel of Fortune, turning slowly and away from you

patron.name: The Curve
patron.pact: It will make you wealthy and it will take thirty years and it will not be interesting for any of them. You may not skip ahead and it knows when you try.

compounder.curse: You will be right, and nobody will be watching at the moment you are proved so.
compounder.bane: A fee expressed as a percentage.

good: A market fell and you did nothing on purpose
You raised the amount going in rather than rearranging what is already there
You could not remember your password because you had not logged in
ill: Rebalancing twice in a quarter
Reading about a fund you already rejected
Explaining compound interest at a dinner nobody invited you to talk at

compounder.reading: Jupiter is slow in your house and that is the whole reading — everything you want is already arriving and none of it will arrive this year. The temptation this season is motion: a tweak, a switch, a clever little optimisation. The single highest-return act available to you has nothing to do with the portfolio and everything to do with what you are paid, and you have not looked at that in four years.

roles.first: Your money's own work outweighs yours, or is on its way to. This is the lever that eventually beats every other one, and it is doing almost nothing visible right now, which is correct and which you will still find hard.
roles.second: It is the quiet half of your plan — the part that keeps going while you are doing something more interesting, and the reason a bad year is survivable rather than fatal.
roles.third: People assume you know about this stuff, and ask you at dinner. Some of that reputation is earned and some of it is that you are willing to say the word 'index' out loud.
roles.shadow: Nothing you own is working. Every pound you have is either spent, sitting, or in bricks, and none of it compounds. Watch for: ten years of good saving that ends up worth less than it started, quietly, in real terms, without anything going wrong.

landholder.headline: You think in bricks.
landholder.coreDesire: To own something real — something that exists when the screen is off and the market is closed.
landholder.coreFear: Paying somebody else's mortgage for thirty years and having nothing at the end to point at.
landholder.truth: It is leveraged, illiquid, occasionally underwater, and it has a boiler. It has made a great many ordinary people wealthy and bankrupted a few of them too.
landholder.atBest: You tolerate slow, lumpy, unglamorous things that other people abandon, and that tolerance is the whole skill. It is why this lever has built more ordinary wealth than any other.
landholder.atWorst: House-poor and entirely concentrated, with a mortgage you call an asset and one tenant you call a portfolio.
landholder.blindSpot: One property is not diversification, and one tenant is not income. When they leave, the whole thing earns zero and the mortgage does not care.

growth.why: Learning liquidity and spread would let you keep the bricks and stop being one bad year from a forced sale.

stress.why: When it is tight, you start nickel-and-diming your own life to feed a building. The house ends up owning you, quietly and by increments.

partner.why: They hold what you cannot — liquid, spread, sellable on a Tuesday. Between you there is almost nothing that could force a sale.

friend.why: They understand wanting a bigger number and they will never tell you property is a scam.

annoying.why: They want returns this quarter. You are on a twenty-year clock and their impatience reads as unseriousness.

wary.why: They can pick up and move countries in a fortnight. You cannot move at all, and some part of you envies that badly.

triggeredBy.why: "Renting is cheaper when you run the numbers." It sometimes is. You will still want to leave the room.

weakTo.why: You built it. Everything you own is one asset, in one place, with one use, and the Golem simply is that fact, standing up.

people.who: An agent who says there is a lot of interest
people.why: There may well be. You will not check, because checking would risk losing it, which is the entire mechanism.

people.who: A relative who bought in 1994 and mentions the price
people.why: They are describing a different country. You will hear a strategy.

people.who: The tenant who is lovely and always late
people.why: You will not enforce it, for months, because the awkwardness is real and the arrears are only numbers.

circumstances.when: A viewing on the first sunny day of the year
circumstances.why: You are not looking at a building. You will find this out in November.

circumstances.when: A fixed rate with under a year left and no plan
circumstances.why: The date arrives whether or not you have thought about it, and thinking about it early is free.

circumstances.when: One empty month
circumstances.why: Your income from it goes to zero and the mortgage does not. One tenant was never a portfolio.

origins.house: The house you had to leave
origins.detail: Somebody else decided when you moved, and you have been buying the ability to say no to that ever since.

origins.house: The house where property was how the family got out
origins.detail: You inherited a story about bricks that is older than you, and it is a good story — it is just not the only one.

origins.house: The house where rent went up every year and nothing was ever yours
origins.detail: You learned what it costs to build somebody else's asset with your wages, and you swore you would not do it twice.

landholder.needsToHear: The building is not the risk. The concentration is. You can keep every brick and still stop being one empty month away from a decision you would not choose.

sign.name: The Foundation
sign.metal: Granite, which is not a metal, and you will not be told otherwise

patron.name: The Deed
patron.pact: Your name on a page, permanent and notarised. In return you may not move quickly, ever, for any reason, including a good one.

landholder.curse: You will own something real and be unable to reach a single pound of it in a week.
resistances: Anybody telling you it is only bricks

good: You priced the voids, the repairs and the tax before you priced the yield
You hold something liquid that is not the building
A tenant renewed without being chased
ill: One tenant described as a portfolio
A fixed rate with under a year on it and no plan
Saying 'it always goes up' out loud, to somebody younger

landholder.reading: Venus in her heavy aspect gives you a genuine gift for permanence, and the bill for it is liquidity. You are standing on something real, which is more than most manage, and you cannot get off it quickly. The work this season is not more bricks. It is the boring liquid thing beside them that means no year, however bad, can ever force your hand.

roles.first: Your wealth is standing somewhere with a roof on it. Slow, lumpy, leveraged, and it has built more ordinary fortunes than every other lever combined — as long as you are never forced to sell it in a hurry.
roles.second: It is the long ambition sitting under the rest of your plan. A part of you is always half-pricing places, even in a year you are not buying.
roles.third: People assume you are settled, sensible and probably doing better than you are. Bricks read as wealth even when they are mostly somebody else's.
roles.shadow: You have no claim on anything physical and no plan to get one. That is a completely legitimate position, right up until it is not chosen. Watch for: thirty years of rent that rises whether or not you do, and nothing at the end of it to point at.

anchor.headline: You buy calm before you buy upside.
anchor.coreDesire: To never be caught short. To be the one person in the family nobody has to worry about.
anchor.coreFear: The drop. The phone call. Needing money you do not have, in front of people.
anchor.lie: I will start investing once I feel safe.
anchor.truth: You will not feel safe. The feeling is not a threshold you cross — it is a setting, and it will move up to meet whatever you have.
anchor.atBest: You are who everyone rings when it goes wrong, and you can absorb a year that would end other people. That is not nothing. That is most of it.
anchor.atWorst: Inflation eats you slowly while you feel responsible about it. You will be the safest person in the room and the poorest one in thirty years.
anchor.blindSpot: Cash feels like safety and behaves like a slow leak. Doing nothing is a decision with a cost; it just never sends you a bill.

growth.why: You already have the temperament — patience, no panic, no need for excitement. You are three decisions away from being extremely good at this and you have made none of them.

stress.why: Fear stops being a floor and becomes a habit. You cut things you can easily afford, and it does not make you feel any safer, so you cut more.

partner.why: You are why they can afford to be wrong, and they are why your safety eventually goes somewhere. Apart you stall and they crash.

friend.why: Neither of you will ever make the other justify not spending money, and that is a rarer comfort than it sounds.

annoying.why: Their appetite for the next number makes your enough look like a lack of ambition, and sooner or later one of them says so out loud.

wary.why: Not because they are reckless. Because a small part of you wonders whether they are living more than you are.

triggeredBy.why: "You are leaving money on the table." You know. You have known for years. Being told does not help and you will not say so.

weakTo.why: It sells you safety, which is the one thing you never negotiate about. You will pay a great deal for a guarantee and never once check what it cost.

people.who: Anybody who says the word “guaranteed” while wearing a suit
people.why: You negotiate on everything except safety, and they know which one they are selling.

people.who: Family, asking
people.why: You are the one with the float. Everyone knows it, and you have never once worked out the number at which you would say no.

people.who: The one doing better who is very relaxed about it
people.why: Their calm makes your carefulness feel like a personality flaw rather than a strategy.

circumstances.when: The first genuinely good year
circumstances.why: Nothing goes wrong, the floor stops feeling urgent, and the money quietly does nothing for twelve months.

circumstances.when: Being told, kindly, that you are being silly
circumstances.why: You will not argue. You will go quiet and do the thing anyway, and resent the person for a year.

circumstances.when: A month where nothing at all goes wrong
circumstances.why: You find it suspicious rather than restful, and you will add to the floor to make the feeling go away.

origins.house: The house where money was there and then suddenly was not
origins.detail: You learned that the floor can go without warning, and no amount of floor has felt like enough since.

origins.house: The house where you were the reliable one before you were old enough for it
origins.detail: Somebody had to hold things steady. You did, and you never really put it down.

origins.house: The house where the number was never said out loud
origins.detail: You could feel it was tight and nobody would confirm it, so you learned to prepare for a danger you were not allowed to see.

anchor.needsToHear: You have built the floor. It is real and it is finished and it is better than most people will ever manage. You are allowed to stand on it now rather than keep making it thicker.

sign.name: The Vault
sign.ruledBy: Saturn, who arrives on time and stays
sign.card: The Four of Pentacles, held close
sign.season: The week after something went wrong

patron.name: The Floor
patron.pact: You will never fall through. You will also never quite be able to stop building it, and no thickness has ever been the last one.

anchor.curse: You will be the safest person in the room and, in thirty years, the poorest one in it.

good: Money left the safe account on purpose and did not come back
You said no to somebody and did not spend the week explaining it
A month where nothing went wrong and you did not find that suspicious
ill: A third emergency fund
Cash sitting past two years untouched
Buying safety from a person in a suit who used the word guaranteed

anchor.reading: Saturn is heavy on you and always has been, which is why you are trusted and why you are tired. The floor is finished. It was finished some time ago and you have been adding to it out of habit rather than need. This season asks the hardest thing available to your sign: to leave it exactly as it is and stand on it. Somebody will call this recklessness. They will be wrong, and they will be the one who is frightened.

roles.first: Your first instinct with money is to make it safe, and it has probably already saved you once. This is the least glamorous lever and the one that decides whether any of the others get to keep running.
roles.second: It is the floor under whatever else you are doing — the reason your risks are survivable and your bad months are only months.
roles.third: People read you as the steady one. They ring you when it goes wrong, and you have never once said no, and some of them have never noticed.
roles.shadow: There is no floor. Everything is deployed, committed, or spent, and a single bad month becomes debt. Watch for: a plan that works perfectly as long as nothing at all happens, and a card balance that appears the first time something does.

speculator.headline: You are comfortable being wrong most of the time for one very good day.
speculator.coreDesire: The bet that changes the shape of your life, not just the size of it.
speculator.coreFear: An ordinary, average, entirely reasonable life that nobody would ever tell a story about.
speculator.lie: I only need to be right once.
speculator.truth: You need to survive being wrong, repeatedly, with enough left to still be at the table. Position size is the whole game and it is the part you find boring.
speculator.atBest: You take the shot nobody else will, sized so that losing it costs you nothing you cannot replace. Done properly this is not gambling — it is the only lever with a genuinely uncapped top end.
speculator.atWorst: Gambling, with a strategy vocabulary. You cannot tell conviction from adrenaline and you have stopped trying.
speculator.blindSpot: You size by excitement rather than by what you could lose. The bet was never the problem — the amount was.

growth.why: A floor does not blunt you, it is what lets you swing properly. Every good risk-taker is boring somewhere, and this is where.

stress.why: When it goes, you have to go back and earn it again — and you will do it fast, badly, and angrily.

partner.why: They are the reason a bad bet is a bad month rather than a bad decade. You will find them frustrating and you will need them enormously.

friend.why: They take real risks too, and they will never make you feel stupid for wanting something bigger than a salary.

annoying.why: They cannot see the upside and they want to talk about your subscriptions while you are trying to describe an asymmetry.

wary.why: They ask what happens if it fails, calmly, and you never have a good answer, and you both notice.

triggeredBy.why: Being told that eight percent a year for thirty years beats you. It might. That is not the objection and you will struggle to say what is.

weakTo.why: It does not sell you a return. It sells you the feeling of being early, which is the one thing you have never learned to price.

people.who: Anyone who tells you that you are early
people.why: It is the only compliment you cannot put down. Early is not a thesis; it is a feeling with a timestamp.

people.who: The friend who won last time
people.why: You will size the next one off their result rather than off what you can afford to lose.

people.who: A confident stranger who is slightly vague on the details
people.why: Vagueness reads as sophistication to you. It almost never is.

circumstances.when: The three days after a win
circumstances.why: You are not calibrated, you are elated, and you will size the next one like the last one already paid for it.

circumstances.when: The three days after a loss
circumstances.why: Doubling feels like conviction and is arithmetic doing the opposite of what you think.

circumstances.when: A Sunday night with nothing to do
circumstances.why: Boredom is the actual entry signal, and it has never once been written down as one.

origins.house: The house where playing it safe did not work either
origins.detail: You watched caution fail to protect somebody, and concluded that if both roads are risky you may as well take the one with a ceiling.

origins.house: The house with one story about somebody who made it
origins.detail: There was a relative, a deal, a moment. It got told often, and it set your idea of what money is for.

origins.house: The house where you were fine and unremarkable
origins.detail: Nothing was wrong, which is its own thing to escape. You are not chasing money so much as evidence of significance.

speculator.needsToHear: Nobody is asking you to stop. Size it so that being wrong five times in a row leaves you standing, and you can keep doing this for forty years instead of four.

sign.name: The Long Odds
sign.ruledBy: A comet, on a schedule nobody has written down
sign.season: The three days after a win

patron.name: The One That Comes Off
patron.pact: It exists. It is real and it does happen. It will not tell you when, and it charges you a stake every single time you ask.

speculator.curse: You will be right once, spectacularly, and unable to say afterwards whether you knew.
vulnerabilities: A friend who won last time

good: You sized it so a total loss changed nothing about your month
You wrote down why before you put money in
You were wrong and it was boring rather than devastating
ill: Doubling after a loss
A stake you would not say out loud to somebody who loves you
Describing a bet as a position and a hope as a thesis

speculator.reading: Your ruling body is a comet and comets are not lucky, they are simply rare and very hard to plan around. Air in cardinal season is enormous initiative and no ballast at all. The reading is not that you should stop — nobody with this chart ever has. It is that the stake, and only the stake, is what decides whether you are doing this at forty. Halve it. The comet does not mind waiting; it has done nothing else.

roles.first: You are playing for the outcome rather than the average, and that is a real strategy — the only one with an uncapped top end. It lives or dies entirely on the size of the stake and you find the stake the boring part.
roles.second: It is the small allocation that keeps you interested in the whole thing. Kept small, it is what stops you meddling with the serious money.
roles.third: People think you are braver than you are. Mostly you just talk about it more than the ones who are actually exposed.
roles.shadow: You never take the shot. Every pound is optimised, defended and accounted for, and none of it is ever pointed at anything with a ceiling. Watch for: a perfectly run life with no upside in it, and a resentment about other people's luck that you would not say out loud.

esotericaNote: The sign, the ruling body, the hour, the metal and the card are invented. They are flavour and they are meant to be enjoyed exactly as much as a star sign is — which is to say properly, and not as information. The people and circumstances are different: those are written from how the lever actually fails, and they are the part worth taking seriously.
bigThreeNote: First, second and third are read off the same ranking the rest of the tool uses — where your money actually moves, or if you have not entered any, how the five questions scored. They are not three separate readings: they are one ranking, shown three deep, and the order genuinely changes when your numbers do. The shadow is the lever at the BOTTOM of that ranking — the one you never pull. It is the most useful of the four and the only one nobody enjoys reading.
